question: Folic acid metabolism is inhibited by :  a) Sulfonamides b) Methotrexate c) Nitrous oxide d) Trimethoprim e) 5–Flucytosine
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Sulfonamides" -> "inhibit dihydropteroate synthase" -> "decreased folate synthesis" -> "inhibited folic acid metabolism" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Methotrexate" -> "inhibits dihydrofolate reductase" -> "reduced conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate" -> "inhibited folic acid metabolism" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Nitrous oxide" -> "oxidizes cobalamin" -> "inhibits methionine synthase" -> "disrupted folate cycle" -> "inhibited folic acid metabolism" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Trimethoprim" -> "inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase" -> "reduced folate production in bacteria" -> "possible effect on human folic acid metabolism" -> 70%
CHAIN: "5-Flucytosine" -> "converted to 5-fluorouracil in fungi" -> "inhibits thymidylate synthase" -> "unclear direct effect on human folic acid metabolism" -> 50%
analysis: Sulfonamides, Methotrexate, and Nitrous oxide are known to inhibit folic acid metabolism through different mechanisms affecting crucial enzymes and biochemical pathways. Trimethoprim and 5-Flucytosine have less direct impact on human folic acid metabolism.
